argument: Given an optimizable metric and an execution environment, an autonomous agent can propose, validate, and iterate scientific solutions that outperform human-designed approaches.
boundary: Evidence is limited to the reported system (EUREKAGENT), tasks (mathematics, kernel engineering, machine learning), and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.
claim: Given an optimizable metric and an execution environment, an autonomous agent can propose, validate, and iterate scientific solutions that outperform human-designed approaches.
conditions: the agent is equipped with capabilities to propose, validate, and iterate solutions
the execution environment supports the required operations
falsifier: One could implement an agent with the described capabilities and test on a held-out set of metric-driven research tasks to verify whether it outperforms human-designed baselines.

title: Provision of an optimizable for production of scientific solutions
